Fix option (b) from bead applied: ChatPatch.message_expiry_seconds changed from Option<u64> to Patch<u64> matching the workspace pattern for nullable patch fields. Spec verified: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 line 505 = 'messageExpirySeconds (UnsignedInt, optional)'. The previous rustdoc claim 'non-nullable' contradicted that.

Handler emission updated to Patch<T>::map_entry() pattern. Two regression tests added covering both Patch::Clear (emits null) and Patch::Set(N) (emits N); Patch::Keep is already covered by the muted-only test which asserts non-Keep fields are absent.

API break: callers using ChatPatch { message_expiry_seconds: Some(N) } must change to Patch::Set(N). From<T> impl on Patch makes the new construction ergonomic. Pre-1.0 so acceptable.

cargo test --workspace green, cargo clippy -p jmap-chat-client --all-targets -- -D warnings clean, cargo fmt clean. Committed as 9655157.
description: src/methods/mod.rs:850-875. ChatPatch.message_expiry_seconds is typed Option<u64> with rustdoc claiming 'Spec defines this as UnsignedInt (non-nullable).' Spec draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 line 505 actually defines messageExpirySeconds as '(UnsignedInt, optional)' — nullable. As Option<u64>, callers can set to Some(N) or omit (no change) but cannot null-clear a previously-set value, which is exactly what an optional/nullable spec field requires. Two possible fixes: (a) if the spec is non-nullable, fix the rustdoc inconsistency; (b) if nullable (which the spec quote suggests), change the field to Patch<u64> so callers can clear. Verify against the spec text and pick one.
title: ChatPatch.message_expiry_seconds rustdoc contradicts spec; field type can't null-clear
